title: Transit Mesh: Cost-First Sidebar and Predictive Route Hints
creator: Ava Chen
description: Proposal for a 'Transit Mesh' information architecture: a compact, cost-first sidebar that surfaces predicted routes (dashboards, rollouts, cost views, and workspace switches) using recent telemetry and keyboard heuristics. The mesh blends a prioritized cost lens with fast-access workspace transit nodes so users can get to their most common actions in 1-2 keystrokes or a single tap. This ticket captures the prototype, design trade-offs, accessibility considerations, and planned engineering handoff artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype (Figma) demonstrates compact sidebar with three prioritized lanes: Cost Lens, Active Rollouts, and Workspace Transit
Keyboard-first flow: Cmd/Ctrl+K opens Transit Mesh and predicts top-5 destinations based on recent activity and role
Cost breakdown chip present on pages and routes into the Cost Lens dashboard with inline rollup metrics
Design passes lightweight usability test with 8 participants showing median task completion time improvement >= 20% for 'find cost per-route' task
Accessible: sidebar meets WCAG 2.1 AA for focus order, contrast, and screenreader labels
Engineering has a documented API contract for telemetry inputs used by prediction heuristics
decisions: Cost-first ordering: place cost lens above other sections to surface economics for every navigation surface. Trade-off: slightly longer path for some non-cost-first tasks; mitigated by predictive routing.
Predictive route heuristic: combine recency, role affinity, and explicit pinned routes. Privacy: only telemetry aggregated per-user and configurable opt-out in settings.
Compact layout: use two-row list items (icon + micro-metrics) to keep height low; trade-off: limited metadata displayed but faster scanning.
Keyboard-centric default: transit mesh opens on Cmd/Ctrl+K; reason: majority of power users prefer keyboard navigation. Also provides mouse affordances for discoverability.
notes_from_research: Early usability (n=5) showed confusion around 'workspace switch' when it lived under a generic account menu; moving a transit node to the top reduced error rate.
Participants expected cost metrics in three places: sidebar summary, per-route header, and dashboard rollup. The mesh provides the summary chip with links to full rollup.
Concerns raised about predictive suggestions leaking sensitive project names; added recommendation for redaction and transparent opt-out in the settings panel.
engineering_considerations: Telemetry contract: recent_routes (array of route keys), role_tags (list), last_active_timestamp (ISO string). Backend to provide top-5 candidates; front-end only ranks and renders.
Performance SLO: sidebar render must not block main thread; implement virtualization for long workspaces list and lazy-load micro-metrics.
A/B plan: server-side flag to toggle Cost-First ordering vs. legacy for 10% of users to validate engagement and task completion metrics.
